feeds.title: U.S Navy Aircraft History
feeds.description: My blog focuses on U.S. Navy Aircraft history. Hi! I'm Tommy H. Thomason. As a young boy in the 50s, I was always enamored with aeroplanes. However, I was not able to be a Naval Aviator because I was nearsighted, I instead became an aeronautical engineer and general aviation pilot. Now retired, I write books and monographs on U.S. Navy aircraft.

feeds.title: Global Maritime History Blogs
feeds.description: Our blogs are a helpful resource to learn about Maritime History. The purpose of GlobalMaritimeHistory.com is to offer maritime historians of all levels and interests a source of information, a route to reach a wide audience for their written work, and a place for congenial discussion.

feeds.title: Civil War Navy
feeds.description: Civil War Navy is a great magazine that will deal with the advancements made in the Naval Warfare during the civil war. We have some of the most knowledgeable civil war experts providing amazing stories and information anxious to help us get started in this adventure.

feeds.title: Naval Historical Foundation Blog
feeds.description: The Naval Historical Foundation blog promotes the mission of NHF and publishes stories about the US Navy Museum and other news from the naval history community. The Naval Historical Foundation preserves and honours the legacy of those who came before us. We educate and inspire the generations who will follow.

feeds.title: Trent Hone
feeds.description: Thoughts on Organizational Learning, Naval History, Doctrine, and Improving Solution Development. Trent Hone is a Vice President with ICF and an award-winning naval historian. He works with organizations to improve their art of practice, increase effectiveness, and accelerate learning.

feeds.title: Soundings in Narragansett Bay's Naval History
feeds.description: This is the Naval War College Museum Blog. Learn about Naval War History here. We are an official Navy museum administered by the Naval History and Heritage Command, the museum features exhibits on the history of naval activity in Narragansett Bay.

feeds.title: Ian M Bates Blog
feeds.description: Ian M Bates writes about Navy history, book reviews, Memoirs & Autobiographies, 18th Century Royal Navy and more in his blog. He is a writer, publisher, and Naval historian.

feeds.title: Houston Maritime Center » Maritime History
feeds.description: Learn about Houston Maritime history, Texas Navy, and battle ships with the help of our blog. Established in 2000, the Houston Maritime Education Center and Museum is an extension of founder James 'Jim' L. Manzolillo's unique experiences, personality, and lifelong association with the ocean.

feeds.title: Sheila Johnson Kindred » Naval History
feeds.description: Sheila Johnson Kindred's blog explores Jane Austen's naval world. After a career in Academia, Sheila pursued her fascination with literature, in particular, the novels of Jane Austen.

feeds.title: Nepeannavalmuseum Blog
feeds.description: Nepean Naval blog tells you our history and stories. We also keep you up to date on what's new and what will be added tp our collection soon. The museum was established in 2015 and its collection of Naval history has been developing and expanding ever since. We are staffed and operated by Ex Servicemen who have a great love and passion to share and preserve their stories.

feeds.title: Naval Historical Society of Australia Blog
feeds.description: The Naval Historical Society of Australia is Preserving Australia's Naval History. Read our blog to learn about the history of Australia's Navy. Our mission is to record, preserve and promote the knowledge, understanding and awareness of naval history of Australia at all levels of the national community.

feeds.title: International Journal of Naval History
feeds.description: The objective of the International Journal of Naval History is to provide a pre-eminent forum for works of naval history researched and written to demonstrable academic standards. Our hope is to stimulate and promote research into naval history and foster communication among naval historians at an international level.
